latest_comment.raw_content:
Dear fellow investors,

It has been a couple of stressful months in the markets.
The good and bad news is that politicians are waking up to the increasing capabilities of AI.

There is also a related, but different, growing worry over data centres, including how they can increase electricity prices and cause other local issues.

Ideally, AI is developed in a safe manner, although slower. That is the best outcome for humanity and the portfolio in the long term.
 
Different companies that are in the 'AI value chain' or in the 'data centre business' now have very different profiles for profitability in the future.
Some have been deservedly knocked down in price, as the political winds have changed and as the interest rate outlook has worsened, among other factors.

Across scenarios, I evaluate that it is best to have a sizeable part of the portfolio invested in the AI value chain, with a bias towards manufacturing companies. This is complemented by having more companies that can do well in scenarios where AI growth is hampered, and in general having more companies with low debt ratios that are less exposed to higher interest rates. 

Best regards,
Jeppe Kirk Bonde
